# Living Context Graphs: Continual Semantic Learning for Enterprise Data Reasoning

## Research question

Persisted business definitions can improve SQL generation but also spread erroneous or stale conventions across later requests.

## Method

Bootstraps semantic objects, writes reusable rule revisions from verified outcomes, and requires model-judged admission before they serve. A separate concept graph routes context using outcome-based allow-list states, freshness checks and a heuristic recovery score; invalidation withdraws routes rather than deleting stored knowledge.

## Evaluation

One fixed Gemini stack uses 353 history and 146 held-out questions from three selected BIRD databases. Every held-out fact has a history teacher. Learning receives answer-match verdicts and retries, while evaluation freezes state. Predicted MySQL row sets are compared with SQLite gold using a 300-second timeout.

## What the results support

Held-out correct answers rise from 20 to 53 of 146; disabling the admission judge reduces this to 29. Disabling final graph routing changes accuracy by at most one question per database while increasing serving cost and latency. Some newly learned rules regress earlier answers.

## Limits and qualifications

The deliberately reachable transfer split is not natural question traffic. Single runs, author fact annotations, strong answer-oracle feedback and unmeasured generator–judge dependence constrain generalization. Recovery counts are correctness flips rather than causal invalidation estimates; claimed checkpoint-noise bounds also conflict with one table transition. No ambiguity, clarification or abstention evaluation is reported.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Provides a concrete context-admission diagnostic and auditable route-state design, without establishing semantic truth, calibrated confidence or robust deployment-time forgetting.
